routes.description: Establish Christian theism as the necessary worldview-level ground of logic, mathematics, knowledge, evidence, and intelligible reality, while showing that the proposed naturalistic foundation cannot account for their universal and necessary scope.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if necessary truths and the conditions of evidence are shown to require an absolute mind identified within Christian theism, and if immediate self-experience or reality alone cannot bridge subjective certainty to universally normative intelligibility.

motionBridge.description: Connect the existence and intelligibility of necessary logical, mathematical, and evidential conditions to the necessary God of Christian theism.

centralBridges.description: Show that reasoning already depends on invariant logic, stable meaning, interpersonal correspondence, and an intelligible reality requiring a worldview-level account.
Establish that necessary logical and mathematical truths are immaterial and require an absolute universal mind rather than merely contingent human descriptions.
Show that certainty about one's own existence does not by itself license conclusions about every possible world or universally normative logical principles.
Maintain the creator–creation and necessary–contingent distinctions needed to block transferring divine explanatory attributes directly to the cosmos.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish contingent linguistic expressions from the necessary truths they express so that descriptions are not conflated with their modal content.
Explain why evidential demands depend on antecedent conditions of intelligibility and therefore cannot be treated as worldview-neutral.

routes.description: Establish that immediate self-experience and reality itself provide a non-theistic basis for intelligibility, with logic, mathematics, and language functioning as derived descriptive systems rather than entities requiring a divine mind.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if self-existence supplies a secure epistemic starting point, objective identity and necessity obtain independently of divine propositions, and adding a sustaining or grounding God contributes no required explanatory condition.

motionBridge.description: Account for logic, mathematics, knowledge, and intelligible reality without requiring Christian theism as their precondition.

centralBridges.description: Ground the epistemic starting point in the impossibility of mistakenly believing that one exists and explain its relevance to logical reasoning.
Establish that reality cannot cease to be reality and that identity and related necessities hold regardless of reality's particular form.
Separate mind-dependent logical and mathematical sentences from the objective realities and relations they accurately describe.
Show that reality can persist by its own nature and that assigning persistence or necessity to God does not require inserting a separate divine sustainer.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish conclusions derived from experience from foundational presuppositions, including logic, mathematics, and linguistic concepts.
Explain why useful epistemic description and interaction need not await an ultimate intrinsic definition of matter or energy.

sections.title: Self-Experience and the Epistemic Starting Point
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether indubitable first-person existence can ground knowledge and logical reasoning without God, or whether an additional principle is required to reach objective and universally normative conclusions.

sections.title: From Identity to Modal and Temporal Necessity
sections.rationale: This section addresses how claims about self-identity and reality's identity extend across possible worlds and time, including the disputed bridge from immediate certainty to necessary logical structure.

sections.title: Necessary Truths, Descriptions, and Ontology
sections.rationale: The distinction between contingent symbols and necessarily accurate logical or mathematical content bears directly on whether such truths require an absolute mind or can describe reality without existing as divine mental objects.

sections.title: Presuppositions and the Intelligibility of Evidence
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether logic, language, correspondence, and evidence are conclusions available from experience or antecedent worldview conditions whose intelligibility requires Christian theism.

sections.title: Reality's Persistence and the Creator–Creation Distinction
sections.rationale: This section captures whether reality needs an external sustainer, whether divine explanatory attributes can be assigned directly to reality, and whether necessary God and contingent creation form a burden-relevant distinction.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-06.proposition: Self-authenticating first-person existence does not by itself establish that the logical and mathematical principles found in one's mind are necessarily descriptive and normative for all reality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-08.proposition: Facts about what a person can believe do not establish what must hold in every possible world unless a connective principle links private thought to necessary truth.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-03.proposition: Reasoning and communication already presuppose invariant identity, stable linguistic meaning, interpersonal correspondence, and an intelligible reality rather than deriving all such conditions from experience.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: God's reality and self-revelation supply the Christian framework within which logic, mathematics, moral realities, mental correspondence, and the unity of reality are intelligible.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: Necessarily true logical and mathematical propositions are immaterial mental objects whose obtaining in every possible world requires an absolute universal mind identified with God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Contingent linguistic expressions must be distinguished from logical and mathematical truths, which obtain necessarily and therefore cannot be treated like contingent words or physical entities.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-05.proposition: Because Christianity distinguishes uncreated God from created reality, attributes assigned to God cannot simply be transferred unchanged to the created cosmos.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-06.proposition: Within the Christian worldview, God is necessary while created reality is contingent, and materialism lacks a ground for the immaterial necessary truths presupposed by meaningful evidence.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-02.proposition: Direct experience requires no antecedent presuppositions, while logic and mathematics can be constructed as formal languages describing experience without depending on God.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-03.proposition: Reality cannot fail to be reality and one plus one cannot fail to equal two even without God, so divine presupposition is not required for those necessities.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-05.proposition: The impossibility of believing that one exists while being wrong supplies a self-validating starting point whose principle applies to thinkers, individual objects, and plurality.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-09.proposition: Logical propositions such as identity statements are mind-dependent sentences, whereas the reality they describe exists objectively, so descriptive success does not require transcendent propositions.

chunk-001:chunk-001-candidate-10.proposition: Nothing, including time or change, can make reality cease to be reality, so identity necessarily holds at every point in the past and future.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-04.proposition: Logic, mathematics, and linguistic concepts are conclusions developed from experience rather than foundational presuppositions, and conversational assumptions do not constitute justificatory premises about reality.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: Objects and relations can exist in mindless worlds even though logic and mathematics are human-created descriptive languages, so their applicability does not imply a divine mind.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: A divine mind is unnecessary to sustain physical reality, because claiming that conceptual truth holds particles in existence lacks evidence and conflates descriptions with what they describe.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-02.proposition: Reality requires no external sustainer because any appeal to God's nature as the reason God persists can apply directly to reality, avoiding both regress and an unnecessary deity.

chunk-003:chunk-003-candidate-07.proposition: The undeniable existence of a thinker capable of being mistaken is sufficient to provide a non-theistic epistemic starting point for knowledge and intelligibility.
